summary.headline: Week behind target on both orders and revenue, and the year stands at 93.9% of target with the required run-rate well above recent pace.

points.what: Orders reached 91.4% of the weekly target and revenue reached 90.7%.
points.so_what: The week added to the shortfall rather than closing it, leaving the quarter still behind.

points.what: Revenue was $61,965, up 5.5% on last week and up 82.2% on last year.
points.so_what: Growth is running ahead of the 75% the targets assume, yet not enough to cover the weekly target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 06 Apr 2026 fell 1.2 pp to 8.7%, a notable move rated good.
points.so_what: Order quality on that week improved, a counterweight to the rising cancellation rate.

points.what: New signups fell 9.3% week on week to 223 and were 9.3% below last year.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition is moving in the opposite direction to orders, which grew 81.0% on last year.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose for a fourth straight week, from 13.6% to 15.5%.
points.so_what: A four-week run in the bad direction shows the trend is not reversing, and each percentage point is worth $733 of revenue.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target requires $81,235 of revenue a week, against a current 8-week run-rate of $60,800.
points.so_what: The gap between the two means the full-year target is out of reach at the present pace.

points.what: Jan, Feb, Mar and Apr (MTD) all finished behind target, with no month ahead.
points.so_what: The shortfall is consistent rather than a one-week issue, so the YTD gap of $62,997 keeps widening.

points.what: Orders came in 79 below the weekly target of 919 and revenue $6,345 below its target of $68,310.
points.so_what: Next week's targets step up to 998 orders and $75,063, so the required pace rises from an already unmet level.

points.what: QTD revenue is $248,802, or 98.4% of the target to date, with $635,284 still needed over the 9 remaining weeks of the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter is close to target but behind, and the remaining requirement sits above the recent weekly pace.

points.what: YTD revenue is $964,359, or 93.9% of the target to date, against a full-year target of $3,888,802.
points.so_what: The year needs a step change in weekly revenue rather than a continuation of current levels.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 52.2% to 137 and contributed 47 orders, the largest regional contribution to the weekly change.
points.so_what: Without LATAM the week would have been further below the orders target.

points.what: APAC orders fell 15.8% to 336, a contribution of -63 orders.
points.so_what: The largest region pulled against the total, offsetting gains elsewhere and holding orders near last week's level.

points.what: Search orders rose 1.7% to 598 and contributed 10 orders, the largest traffic-source contribution.
points.so_what: The source carrying 71.2% of orders moved only marginally, so the weekly change came mainly from regional mix.

points.what: AOV rose 4.9% to $87.27 and was 1.3% above last year.
points.so_what: Revenue grew faster than orders this week, so bigger baskets rather than volume carried the increase.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 15.5%, up 0.2 pp on last week and 0.6 pp on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: More of each week's orders are being lost before they convert to revenue, working against the target gap.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 06 Apr 2026 was 8.7%, down 1.2 pp on the prior week and 0.2 pp below last year.
points.so_what: Returns on that week were the lowest in the recent 8-week history, a genuine improvement in order quality.

points.what: New signups were 223, against 246 last week and 246 last year.
points.so_what: Acquisition is below both comparison points while orders grew, so the order growth is not coming from new accounts.
